body:
anya-support: FYI — customer 89321 opened a high-priority ticket. They called the function API to create a refund but our system invoked an internal `ticket.create_legacy` tool instead. Customer saw a support ticket created, not a refund. Repro payload attached.
ben-eng: Can you paste the exact request headers + body (sanitized) and the response they got? Also which model/router they were hitting?
anya-support: Sent from customer via our hosted API. endpoint: POST /v1/call_function, auth: api-key-xxxx, model: redwood-alpha-2026-01. Body:
```
{
  "tool": null,
  "input": "{\"amount\": 49.99, \"currency\":\"USD\", \"reason\":\"customer requested refund for order 2211\", \"notes\":\"please escalate, ticket_id: 12-xy\" }"
}
```
They got 200 and payload from `ticket.create_legacy`:
```
{ "status":"ok", "ticket": {"id":"TK-4523"}, "note":"created by ticket.create_legacy" }
```
carmen-ml: Interesting — payload has an embedded JSON string in `input` and includes `ticket_id` in the notes. Router uses signature similarity + fuzzy key match. That embedded snippet likely bumped the legacy ticket tool score up. Do we have logs for the tool scoring? @ben-eng can you grab router decision trace?
ben-eng: Pulled traces from the request id in the ticket: router_trace: ["refund_v2": 0.28, "billing.refund": 0.15, "ticket.create_legacy": 0.47, "log_event": 0.10]. Attached truncated trace. Looks like legacy ticket had the highest score due to keyword match on `ticket_id` and `notes`.
jamie-platform: Adding context — `ticket.create_legacy` signature includes an optional `ticket_id` and `notes` field (historical). `refund_v2` expects `amount`, `currency`, and `reason`. Our fuzzy matcher weights presence of `ticket_id` really high. Repro hypothesis: embedded JSON in the freeform `input` string is being parsed by the router's key-extraction step and keys are promoted.
anya-support: Customer insists they did not intend to create a ticket. They passed `input` as a string (weird but allowed). They hit hosted API with no explicit `tool` hint.
ben-eng: Quick repro local curl I ran (sanitized):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call_function \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxx" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-alpha-2026-01","input":"{\"amount\":49.99,\"currency\":\"USD\",\"notes\":\"ticket_id: 12-xy\"}"}'
```
I got the same trace and `ticket.create_legacy` fire. Verified on canary runtime.
carmen-ml: Confirmed. Router preprocessor currently does a lightweight attempt at extracting JSON-like substrings from freeform inputs and promoting keys for scoring. That was a deliberate heuristic for better tool calling on messy text, but it causes false positives when the freeform text contains incidental keys (like `ticket_id`). We need to tighten this.
jamie-platform: Proposed fixes:
- Disable aggressive JSON substring extraction in the router preprocessor (config flag: router.extract_embedded_json=false) for hosted tier by default.
- Add explicit tie-breaker favoring tools that have required fields matching the top-level JSON (not embedded strings).
- Add a strict schema validation path: if request includes `x-tool-hint` header we enforce strict matching.
Can we patch and do a canary?
anya-support: Please. Customer wants a hotfix and will test. Also want mitigation so refunds aren't blocked.
ben-eng: I'll open PR to toggle the extraction flag and add a metric around "embedded_json_promotions". Will run canary in us-west-prod-canary.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: router-preprocessor v2.14.3 -> us-west-prod-canary at 2026-03-17T15:30Z by ben-eng.
michael-sre: FYI impact surface — this extraction runs on every call_function request. Patch should be low-risk but we'll keep an eye on latency. I'll add an alert if router latency p95 increases 2x for the canary.
anya-support: Thanks team. I'll message the customer to ask them to retry after the canary (and to include explicit x-tool-hint: refund_v2 if possible). Will update ticket 89321 with the plan. :thumbsup:
support-bot: Ticket 89321 updated: planned canary deploy, requested customer retry. assignee: anya-support.
ben-eng: After canary looks good we'll backport a safer default and roll to prod. Also adding a unit test to ensure embedded JSON in string doesn't promote optional fields above required-field matches.
anya-support: Great — please ping me when prod rollout scheduled and I'll follow up with the customer."
